title: Dynamic Bayesian Network modelling of psychopathology during outpatient treatment
summary: In clinical medicine, it is often assumed that illnesses can be traced back to an underlying, identifiable cause (e.g. certain symptoms may arise when an infection is the cause). However, in the case of a mental disorder, it can be helpful to view a disorder as a pattern  of symptom interactions. The symptoms of a mental disorder can therefore be understood as a network of symptoms that influence each other over time. It is the pattern of symptoms that constitutes the mental illness observable from the outside (e.g. if joylessness, lack of motivation and depressed mood exist and maintain each other, this is referred to as a disorder). This study aims to observe precisely these links and connections between symptoms during psychotherapy. This study will examine in more detail whether recurring patterns of these temporal links can be identified, whether they are characterized by certain central or heralding symptoms, whether they are associated with a better outcome at the end of therapy, and finally, whether certain characteristics of the patients influence these patterns.

interventions.name: Retrospective analysis of all adult patients of the outpatient clinic of the TU Braunschweig from 2015 - 2025.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Adult patients who underwent therapy with at least 5 sessions between 2015 and 2025 at the psychotherapy outpatient clinic of the TU Braunschweig.
Exclusion criteria:
Insufficient or insufficiently consistent values.
